chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from some of his companions, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him: A man had two witnesses testify that he owed a man fifty dirhams, and then two others came and testified that he owed him one hundred dirhams. All of them testified in the same setting. He said: 'Cast lots among them, then make those selected by the lot swear by God that they are testifying to the truth.'
ai.seo_question: How does Shia jurisprudence resolve conflicting witness testimonies for different debt amounts?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the application of the 'Qar'' (lot-casting) method in Shia jurisprudence to resolve contradictory testimonies of equal weight, a principle notably discussed by scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Tusi in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*. By selecting one pair of witnesses via lot and then administering an oath, the court establishes the debt based on the presumption of truthfulness for the chosen group, reflecting a pragmatic approach to evidentiary uncertainty in civil disputes.
